title: Sentinel KB embedding strategy + hosting decision - discovery
topics: hosting: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
summary: Customer Sentinel Labs is evaluating an embeddings + rerank pipeline for a knowledge base product. They need guidance on embedding dimension, routing vs rerank, and whether to run on Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private VPC given compliance and throughput needs. Agreed to run a focused throughput benchmark and pilot with a 10k-doc sample and follow up with security docs and pricing options.
next_steps: Redwood: share Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pricing and perf matrix (Maya) by 2026-12-07
SE: propose benchmark plan and test dataset, run initial latency smoke test (Jonah) by 2026-12-10
Customer: share sample dataset and current ES + vector DB schema (Priya) by 2026-12-06
action_items: Maya Chen: Send security pack + SOC2 summary (due 2026-12-07)
Jonah Patel: Benchmark plan + run initial 1k qps stress test on Hosted (due 2026-12-10)
Priya Rao: Export 10k-doc sample and schema, share S3 link (due 2026-12-06)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Head of Search, Sentinel Labs), Alex Morton (CTO), Samir Khan (Data Eng)
Links shared: Redwood hosting deck https://redwood.example/deck, perf spreadsheet https://sheets.example/redwood-sentinel-bench

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh, really appreciate it. quick intros?
[00:10] Priya Rao: sure, i'm priya, i run the search team at sentinel, we power the KB for support and product docs, and we ship a relevance layer on top of ES.
[00:18] Alex Morton: alex, cto, i'm here to watch infra implications and cost.
[00:22] Samir Khan: samir, data eng, i'll own the embedding pipeline and vector db sync.
[00:28] Maya Chen: great. jonah from our infra team?
[00:31] Jonah Patel: hey all, jonah, solutions eng, i'll cover perf/throughput and ops stuff.

[00:45] Maya Chen: priya, can you give a quick picture of current stack and pain points?
[00:50] Priya Rao: yeah. so right now search is elasticsearch for classic term match. we started using pinecone for a pilot but hit tail latency and costs as we scale. our users need sub-200ms median for retrieval+rerank, ideally < 400ms p99. currently rerank happens in-app using a smaller LM which is slow at scale.
[01:20] Samir Khan: also we have multi-tenant data residency needs, some datasets can't leave region for compliance, so that influences hosting.
[01:30] Jonah Patel: okay, so two axes: latency/throughput economics and hosting compliance. what are your qps numbers now and target?
[01:39] Priya Rao: baseline is about 80 qps avg but peaks up to 700 qps for certain support spikes, sustained bursts for 2-5 minutes.
[01:48] Alex Morton: our goal is handling 1k burst for 10 minutes with graceful degradation, not full fail.

[02:00] Maya Chen: perfect. on the architecture side, are you leaning toward embedding-only retrieval with a reranker or hybrid term+vector with rerank?
[02:09] Priya Rao: our initial eval indicated hybrid search gets better precision on intent queries; embedding dims and size of vectors were a question. we tried 1536 dims and it was heavier. curious about compact embeddings 768 or even 384. tradeoffs?
[02:27] Jonah Patel: shorter dims obviously reduce storage and vector DB throughput, but can be lower recall for nuanced KB content. we usually measure recall-at-k across representative queries. for many KBs 768 hits a good balance; 384 sometimes works for short-span content but needs careful retrain. misspell: our own customers call it "compatic embeddings" sometimes, sorry.
[02:48] Priya Rao: heh. ok. what about rerank model placement? Run rerank on the host that serves traffic or in a dedicated batch tier?
[02:56] Jonah Patel: depends on latency SLOs. if you need sub-200ms for user-facing, you likely do vector retrieval in the edge/dedicated pool and do a light rerank model in the same path. heavier reranks can happen async or fallback to cached results. Redwood's dedicated pools can pin capacity for consistent tail-latency. Hosted can work but may hit noisy neighbors at extreme bursts unless you reserve dedicated capacity.

[03:30] Maya Chen: security side—Priya mentioned residency. do you have SOC2 reqs or SSO/KMS?
[03:36] Priya Rao: SOC2 yes, we need audit logs, SSO via SAML, and keys must be customer managed for certain datasets (so KMS or HSM).
[03:46] Maya Chen: we do SOC2 and provide audit logs; private deployment supports customer KMS and full VPC peering. we can also offer Dedicated with VPC egress control. i'll send the packet.

[04:05] Samir Khan: on vector DB integration—what patterns do you recommend? keep ES for term and Pinecone for vectors, or consolidate?
[04:13] Jonah Patel: common is hybrid: ES for exact matches and filter predicates, vector DB for semantic fanout. You can run a cascade: ES filter -> vector fanout -> rerank. Alternatively, some customers try to add vectors as a plugin into ES or use a single-store vector DB like weaviate. tradeoffs: single store simplifies ops, but sometimes specialized vector DBs give better throughput and sharding options.
[04:38] Priya Rao: latency wise, for rerank we saw vector+rerank was doubling response times in our pilot. curious what Redwood's caching/kv strategies are.
[04:47] Jonah Patel: Redwood runtime has prefix KV caching and dynamic batching which reduces per-token cost and latency; for embeddings/rerank we recommend caching top-k vectors and using warmup for typical queries. also routing policies: can route to cheaper model variant for non-critical routes, fall back to smaller model under pressure. note: my keyboard typed k-v cash earlier, transcription is messy.

[05:15] Alex Morton: burst capacity—can you explain how Dedicated bursting vs Hosted burst works?
[05:20] Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity you can autoscale within a pool and set burst policies; it's predictable and good when you want tail SLOs. Hosted is elastic but subject to regional capacity; it has cheaper entry but less predictable tail for intense bursts. Private gives you VPC control and on-prem options for full data residency.

[06:00] Priya Rao: ok, concrete numbers: if we pick 768-dim embeddings and 10 million vectors, what order of magnitude for storage and token cost?
[06:10] Jonah Patel: rough guestimate: 768 dims float16 quantized -> ~1.5KB per vector; 10M -> ~15GB raw plus index overhead x2-3 depending on index type -> 30-45GB. throughput: optimized quantized runtime gives you ~2-3x better per-GPU throughput vs full float. we'll put numbers in the perf sheet.

[06:45] Samir Khan: index sharding: we need advice on shard counts and fanout to keep p99 low.
[06:51] Jonah Patel: we typically recommend shard per 1-2 billion vectors per shard? wait that's huge, scratch that: for your scale, multiple shards per node tuned to latency, and tune fanout topk to balance recall. we'll provide a sharding playbook in the follow-up doc.

[07:15] Priya Rao: what about rerank model size? is it common to use a 7B or do smaller cross-encoders suffice?
[07:21] Jonah Patel: for rerank, lightweight cross-encoder models (few hundred million to 1.3B) often hit the sweet spot for latency. 7B yields higher quality but needs dedicated GPUs and affects cost. Redwood Optimize can recommend model quantization for your workload.

[07:50] Maya Chen: timeline and success metrics—what would a pilot look like?
[07:54] Priya Rao: pilot objective is: demonstrate 4x cost improvement over current pinecone+rerank baseline at equal or better recall@10, and p99 <= 400ms for user-facing routes. timeline: pilot in 4-6 weeks.

[08:10] Jonah Patel: propose: 1) you share 10k-doc sample + canonical queries, 2) we run Hosted bench for retrieval latency and throughput at target qps, 3) run Dedicated sim with pinned capacity to show tail-latency benefits, 4) run a rerank variant with 1.3B quantized model to show tradeoffs.

[08:37] Alex Morton: cost controls—how granular is cost attribution? we need per-route and per-token breakdowns.
[08:44] Maya Chen: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and tags can map to product teams. We'll show a sample invoice and cost dashboard.

[09:00] Priya Rao: about private deployment—if some datasets must remain in-region, can we run a hybrid where the private deployment handles sensitive subsets and hosted handles public docs?
[09:10] Jonah Patel: yes, hybrid routing is common: route sensitive queries to Private VPC nodes; route everything else to Hosted or Dedicated. We can set policy-based routing by customer id or dataset tag.

[09:28] Samir Khan: ops question: how do we keep vector sync between ES and vector DB, and handle stale embeddings?
[09:34] Jonah Patel: we recommend an incremental pipeline with change capture, background re-embed for updated docs, and staleness detection with TTL. Redwood's SDK supports async batch embedding and reingestion; we'll share a sample connector.

[10:00] Priya Rao: okay, real world worry: we did a test and saw p99 spikes with cold kv cache; how to mitigate?
[10:08] Jonah Patel: prewarm strategies, keep a hotset cache for popular queries, and set autoscale thresholds to kick in early. Also model-variant fallback gives graceful degradation.

[10:30] Maya Chen: any regulatory concerns—we support KMS and customer-managed keys on Private, right?
[10:35] Jonah Patel: yes, KMS/HSM integrations for Private, Dedicated supports customer KMS via cloud KMS integrations and audit logs. We'll include deployment diagrams.

[11:00] Priya Rao: ok, can you outline the minimal data we need to run the benchmark?
[11:05] Jonah Patel: sample: 10k documents with canonical id, text body, metadata filters; a query set of 1k canonical queries with expected relevance labels; traffic pattern description (p50/p95/p99 targets and burst patterns). CSV or ndjson ok.

[11:28] Alex Morton: what about SSO for our team? SAML and role-based access controls?
[11:33] Maya Chen: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC with fine-grained roles, and audit export.

[11:45] Priya Rao: cost and procurement—if we do Dedicated, what's lead time?
[11:49] Maya Chen: Dedicated usually needs a short provisioning window, 2-3 weeks for pool sizing and commit setup. Private on-prem is longer. Pricing sheet will have commit tiers.

[12:05] Samir Khan: are there customers who keep ES as primary and do vector lookup as secondary pattern? any benchmarks?
[12:13] Jonah Patel: yes that's common; we'll share a case study where hybrid reduced false-positives 18% and improved median latency.

[12:35] Priya Rao: for our pilot, we want to see 768 dims, then test 1536 for recall delta. can you run both?
[12:42] Jonah Patel: yep, we'll run dims 384/768/1536 sampling and produce recall/throughput curves.

[13:00] Maya Chen: ok, recap and next steps: i'll send security docs and pricing, jonah will own benchmark plan, priya will share dataset. we tentatively target pilot kickoff week of 2026-12-15.

[13:18] Priya Rao: sounds good. quick Q: any blockers on our side to use Hosted for initial bench?
[13:23] Maya Chen: none, Hosted is quickest to spin up. If you need strict residency for the sample data we can s3 in-region or use Private for the pilot.

[13:35] Alex Morton: last question, SLA for Dedicated?

[13:38] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA windows and higher support tiers; we'll include SLA targets in pricing packet.

[13:48] Samir Khan: thanks, that was helpful, we'll share dataset by monday.

[13:55] Maya Chen: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with notes and links.

[14:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-attributions and transcription errors (k-v cash/k-v cache, compatic embeddings). Natural speech filler and interruptions preserved.
